problems.title: Roots in a two-to-one ratio
problems.question: The roots of x²−6x+c=0 have ratio 2:1. Find their product.
problems.idea: Use exact identities and check all constraints before choosing an answer.
formulas: Let the roots be 2t, t. Vieta gives $3t=6$.
steps: t=2, so the roots are 4,2 and their product 8.

problems.title: Consecutive binary numbers
problems.question: Which printed binary triple gives consecutive natural numbers?
problems.idea: Use exact identities and check all constraints before choosing an answer.
formulas: Binary place values are powers of 2.
steps: The triple 10111,11000,11001 represents 23,24,25. The other listed triples skip or reverse at least one integer.

problems.title: Simplify before squaring
problems.question: Evaluate $(\sqrt{20}+\sqrt{80}-\sqrt{125})^2$.
problems.idea: Use exact identities and check all constraints before choosing an answer.
steps: The inner sum is(2+4−5)√5=√5. Square it.

problems.title: Tangential trapezoid perimeter
problems.question: An isosceles trapezoid has obtuse angle 150° and incircle radius 2. Find its perimeter.
problems.idea: Use exact identities and check all constraints before choosing an answer.
formulas: The height is $2r=4$. Its acute angle is 30°, so a leg is $4/\sin30°=8$.
steps: For a tangential quadrilateral the base sum equals the leg sum,16. Thus the full perimeter is 16+16.

problems.title: Nonempty intersection of root sets
problems.question: Find the product of a values for which |x−3|=a−5 has a solution in common with(x²−6x+5)(x−3)=0.
problems.idea: Use exact identities and check all constraints before choosing an answer.
formulas: The second root set is $\{1,3,5\}$. At those roots, $|x-3|$ is 2,0,2.
steps: Thus a−5 must equal 0 or 2, giving a=5 or 7. Their product is 35.

problems.title: A squared absolute value
problems.question: Find the root sum of |x−5|²=9.
problems.idea: Use exact identities and check all constraints before choosing an answer.
steps: The roots are 2 and 8. Add them.

problems.title: Rationalise three denominators
problems.question: Evaluate $5/\sqrt{18}+1/(6-3\sqrt2)-1/(\sqrt2+1)$.
problems.idea: Use exact identities and check all constraints before choosing an answer.
steps: Add the first two terms:√2+1/3. Subtract√2−1, cancelling the radical.

problems.title: Minimum of a quotient over a box
problems.question: Minimise ab/c for −3≤a≤6,−4≤b≤5,2≤c≤9.
problems.idea: Use exact identities and check all constraints before choosing an answer.
formulas: The smallest ab is −24, attained at a=6, b=−4. With a negative numerator, dividing by the smallest positive c makes the quotient least.
steps: Choose c=2. The resulting value is −24/2. Nonnegative products cannot give a smaller value.

problems.title: Sum of parallelogram diagonals
problems.question: Sides are √12 and √28. One diagonal is 4 longer than the other. Find their sum.
problems.idea: Use exact identities and check all constraints before choosing an answer.
steps: (p+q)²=2(p²+q²)−(p−q)²=160−16=144. The sum is positive.

problems.title: Position of a trapezoid section
problems.question: A trapezoid’s bases are BC=6, AD=16. A parallel section MN=10 meets CD at N. Find CN: ND.
problems.idea: Use exact identities and check all constraints before choosing an answer.
formulas: At fraction t from BC toward AD the width is $6+t(16-6)$.
steps: Set 10=6+10t, giving t=2/5. Thus CN: ND=t:(1−t)=2:3.

problems.title: Two complementary trigonometric squares
problems.question: Evaluate $1/(1+\tan^247°)+\cos^243°$.
problems.idea: Use exact identities and check all constraints before choosing an answer.
steps: The expression is cos²47°+sin²47°.

problems.title: A linear inequality in an absolute value
problems.question: Solve $|x-4|-(2|x-4|-1)/3<3$.
problems.idea: Use exact identities and check all constraints before choosing an answer.
steps: This simplifies to t<8, or −8<x−4<8. Add 4.

problems.title: Two quadratic branches
problems.question: Find the sum of roots of |x−3|=|x²−5|.
problems.idea: Use exact identities and check all constraints before choosing an answer.
steps: The first quadratic x²−x−2=0 has roots 2,−1 with sum 1. The second x²+x−8=0 has two real roots with sum −1. The branches have no common root, since a common root would require x=3 and x²=5 simultaneously. Add the sums.

problems.title: A parallel section length
problems.question: MN∥AC cuts BC at N with BN: NC=4:5. AC=27. Find MN.
problems.idea: Use exact identities and check all constraints before choosing an answer.
steps: Multiply 27 by 4/9.

problems.title: Geometric mean altitude
problems.question: ABC is right at C, with altitude CD to AB. AD=a, BD=b, AC=6, BC=8. Find 5√ab.
problems.idea: Use exact identities and check all constraints before choosing an answer.
steps: Thus √ab=CD=24/5. Multiply by 5.

problems.title: Reciprocal trigonometric roots
problems.question: A quadratic ax²+bx+c=0 has roots tanα and cotα for an acute α. Which coefficient relation is necessary?
problems.idea: Use exact identities and check all constraints before choosing an answer.
steps: Therefore c=a.

problems.title: Count integers in a linear system
problems.question: How many integers satisfy 2x−1≤12 and 4x+3≥−1?
problems.idea: Use exact identities and check all constraints before choosing an answer.
steps: The integers are −1,0,1,2,3,4,5,6.

problems.title: Six trigonometric equalities
problems.question: How many of the six printed equalities are identities for acute α?
problems.idea: Use exact identities and check all constraints before choosing an answer.
steps: Equality 1 follows because(2cos²α+1)/cos²α=2+sec²α=3+tan²α. Equalities 2,3,5 follow directly from the listed rules. Equality 6 is expansion of(sinα+cosα)².
Equality 4 cancels 3(sinα−cosα)/[6(sinα−cosα)]=1/2 wherever defined, but it is undefined at α=45°. Thus all 6 are identities on their own domains; only 5 are defined and true for every acute α.
problems.answer: 6 on the common defined domain;5 if “for every acute angle” includes 45°.
problems.note: The fourth equality has a zero denominator at 45°. The domain convention changes the count, so both interpretations are explained.

problems.title: A triangle forced to be obtuse
problems.question: Positive lengths a, b for m a triangle with sides 3a+2b,2a+4b,5a+5b. Which property is necessary?
problems.idea: Use exact identities and check all constraints before choosing an answer.
formulas: The largest side is z=5a+5b. The cosine rule makes its opposite angle obtuse exactly when $z^2>(3a+2b)^2+(2a+4b)^2$.
steps: Subtracting the right side gives 12a²+22ab+5b², strictly positive for a, b>0. The triangle inequalities also hold since the two smaller sides sum to 5a+6b>z.

problems.title: A possible triangle perimeter
problems.question: Each side of a triangle is a root of(x²−8x+15)(x−7)(x²−2x+1)=0. Which listed perimeter is possible?
problems.idea: Use exact identities and check all constraints before choosing an answer.
formulas: The positive roots are $1,3,5,7$. Every side is odd, so the sum of three sides is odd.
steps: Of4,8,10,17,16,24 only 17 is odd. It is attainable, for example by sides 5,5,7, which satisfy 5+5>7.

problems.title: Exactly one permitted rational root
problems.question: Find the least a such that $(x^2-4x+a)/(x^2-1)=0$ has exactly one real solution.
problems.idea: Use exact identities and check all constraints before choosing an answer.
formulas: The domain excludes x=±1. The numerator has a repeated root at a=4. It has a root at 1 when a=3 and at −1 when a=−5.
steps: For a=4, the sole root is 2. For a=3, roots 1,3 leave only 3. For a=−5, roots −1,5 leave only 5. For every other a<4 both real roots are permitted; for a>4 there are none. The least of −5,3,4 is −5.

problems.title: A quadratic polynomial remainder
problems.question: Find the remainder of x⁴−x³+6x−4 divided by x²−2x+3.
problems.idea: Use exact identities and check all constraints before choosing an answer.
steps: Substitute:(−4x−3)−(x−6)+6x−4=x−1.

problems.title: Equivalent root sets
problems.question: For which a are $(x^2-5x+6)(x^2-5x)=0$ and $|x^2-5x+a|=a$ equivalent?
problems.idea: Use exact identities and check all constraints before choosing an answer.
formulas: Put $t=x^2-5x$. The first equation allows t=0 or −6. For a≥0 the second allows t=0 or −2a.
steps: The first root set is{0,2,3,5}. To include x=2 or 3, the second must allow t=−6, giving a=3. At a=3 its two allowed t values are exactly 0 and −6, so the solution sets agree.

problems.title: A circle crossing a right trapezoid
problems.question: Right trapezoid ABCD has A=B=90°. A circle through A, D, C meets leg AB at E, with AE=6, BE=2 and CD=10. Find CE.
problems.idea: Use exact identities and check all constraints before choosing an answer.
formulas: Take $A=(0,0),B=(0,8),D=(d,0),C=(c,8),E=(0,6)$. The circle through A, D, E has equation $x^2+y^2-dx-6y=0$.
steps: Substituting C gives c(d−c)=16. Also CD²=(d−c)²+64=100, so |d−c|=6. Since c>0 and c(d−c)>0, d−c=6 and c=8/3.
CE²=c²+(8−6)²=64/9+4=100/9. Take the positive root.

problems.title: A circle through three bisector feet
problems.question: AB=BC=1. Bisectors AE, BD, CF meet opposite sides at E, D, F. B lies on the circle through D, E, F. Find AC.
problems.idea: Use exact identities and check all constraints before choosing an answer.
formulas: Put AC=b and let half the apex angle B be θ. Then $BD=\cos\theta$, $b=2\sin\theta$, and the bisector theorem gives $BE=BF=1/(1+b)$.
steps: E, F are symmetric about BD. Hence the circle through B, D, E, F has its centre on BD, which makes BD a diameter. Thus BED=90°. In right triangle BED, BE=BDcosθ=cos²θ.
Therefore 1/(1+b)=1−b²/4. Multiply and simplify: b(b²+b−4)=0. Since b>0, solve b²+b−4=0 and choose the positive root. It is less than 2, as required for base b with equal sides 1.
